hub.title: The Eligian Tour
hub.tagline: A presentation that teaches the language it is written in.

hub.tagline: Een presentatie die de taal uitlegt waarin ze is geschreven.

operationData.template: This line lives in hint.html. A named import read it at compile time, and setElementContent(@hint) placed it here.

actionOperationData.template: An Eligian presentation is one or more timelines. Here's the one you're watching.
its name — also what navigate and the engine's uri use
What advances the timeline? Its provider — and the header can loop it or fix its duration.
raf = animation clock · video / audio drive from media · scroll = the scroll position · custom
Inside a timeline, at schedules work over a time range: start to end, or start for a duration.
a time range: start .. end — or start for duration
Times take units. No unit means seconds — and in arithmetic a bare number is a factor.
Ranges can compute — and chain off the previous event with a +.
relative time — anchored to the previous event's end
Name a time once with const, label an event with as, and later times refer to them. This chapter is timed exactly that way.
@beat is a compile-time constant · open.end refers to an earlier event of this timeline
target selects an element for a block's start and its end — and an inline end block is optional.
selectElement at the head of both blocks; nothing carries from start to end
That whole chapter? One timeline: on enter shows it, on leave cleans up, neither counts toward its 58 seconds, and its beats are timed with a constant and labels. Hub, space pauses, r replays.
one open-ended action { start: 0 }, not counted in the duration · on leave runs on navigate / stop, not when the content ends
An action is a named list of operations. Define once, call anywhere.
declares a reusable action; its body runs top-to-bottom
Actions take parameters. Annotate types when you want the compiler's help — or leave the type off.
optional type — string · number · boolean · object · array; no annotation = unchecked
Inside a block, calling your action looks exactly like calling a built-in operation.
one syntax: action first, then built-in op; a bare operation is not a timeline event
Parameters flow into operations by name — and when the names differ, the compiler bridges them.
same name → passed straight through · other name → a setOperationData before the operation
An endable action has two blocks: set up, then tear down — independently.
start & end run separately — re-select in each, or use target
The compiler knows what each block carries. Call an action that needs a selected element where there is none, and it tells you.
an inferred contract — the hover says Requires from the caller
selectElement consumes its selector. Your parameter survives anyway: the compiler saves and restores it.
saved as __eligian_param_selector around the operation; found by eligian smoke · a parameter that reaches a selector is checked at every call (spec 056)
Group actions into a library and import what you need — renamed if you like. Chapter 05 goes deeper. Hub.
const names a value. Known at compile time it is inlined wherever you write @name; a runtime value becomes a scope variable.
@name reads a const · literal → folded in · runtime value → scope variable
Values are literals: strings in either quote, numbers, booleans, null, objects and arrays.
no negative literals: -2 is unary minus applied to 2
Operators fold at compile time. On runtime values they belong in if conditions — except string +, which joins at runtime.
if / else if / else runs operations conditionally — when, otherwise, endWhen, nested.
else if = else { if … }: a when nested in the otherwise
for iterates a collection — and this list is being revealed by one right now.
@@p is the loop item (= @@currentItem); @@loopIndex / @@loopLength count
continue skips an item, break leaves the loop — only inside a for. Watch 0 skipped and the run stop at 12.
continue → continueForEach · break → breakForEach · outside a for: compile error
with selects an element for a block, in any action or event — this tour's clearSpots is two with blocks.
the selection stays after the block — there is nothing to restore
Where data lives: $operationdata, $globaldata, $scope — and the short forms you have been reading. Hub.
Scheduling a chain of events by hand means recomputing every time you tweak one.
change one length and every later time is re-done by hand
'sequence' lays events back-to-back automatically — each runs 'for' a duration.
start = previous end → 0s..5s · 5s..15s · 15s..18s
Because starts are computed, changing one duration shifts everything after it.
shorten 'main' and 'outro' slides left — no re-numbering
'stagger' fans one effect across a collection — each item starts a little after the last.
200ms between starts · the item is the action's first argument · at editBeat.end anchors the first item
A sequence item can be an inline block, labelled with as; each runs before every item, then after it. each clears the spotlights; then flips this dot at the end of every beat.
each → before every item's start ops · then → after every item's end ops, in the same instant as the next each · editBeat.end usable later
The inline stagger form has its own start and end blocks, and at anchors the first item on a time instead of the previous event. Watch the wave.
every block starts empty: selectElement(@@item) first · at +2s would count from the previous event
sequence for distinct back-to-back steps; stagger for one effect across many items. Hub.
An .eligian file is a program — timelines, actions, imports — or a library that starts with library and holds only actions.
a library may import other libraries; no timelines, consts or assets; it cannot be compiled on its own
languages comes first: the codes, their labels, and a star on the default. One entry is its own default.
xx-XX codes, unique; compiles to language + availableLanguages
Four default imports, one of each: layout, styles, provider, locales. Paths are relative to the file.
one of each per file; ./ or ../ only — no absolute paths or URLs
A named import gives an asset a name. An HTML file becomes a string you can place with @name.
names are unique per file; contextual keywords allowed as names
import { … } from a library: public actions by name, renamed with as. private keeps a helper at home.
errors: private import, missing action, name clash with an operation or a local action, circular libraries
extensions declares your own JavaScript: operations, controllers and functions the module exports. The compiler trusts the declaration; the bundle carries the module.
one per program; .js .mjs .ts .mts .jsx .tsx; no Eligius names; params name, name?, name: type
Comments: // and /* */. A /** doc */ with @param above an action becomes hover documentation.
typing /** + Enter above an action fills the template (Chapter 07)
Sixteen reserved words can't be names. Every other keyword is contextual — fine as a parameter or const; action names are stricter. Hub.

reserved: action break const continue else endable false for if import null on sequence stagger timeline true · action names accept fewer: plain names and the verbs (play, toggle, run, key, …), so action loop() fails (Chapter 07)
Everything so far fired on the clock. A presentation also reacts — to clicks, keys, events, and to your own code. That's engine reach.
five doors past the clock
broadcastEvent puts a message on the engine's bus. Whoever listens for that name reacts: your on event handlers, controllers — and the engine itself.
one bus, many listeners; request-timeline-uri is a broadcast the engine answers by switching
An on event action runs when its event fires, not at a time. Click the button: it broadcasts tour-ping, and this handler reveals the panel.
params map to eventArgs by position · topic "x" namespaces · parentheses optional with no params
on <event> on an element runs a verb: navigate, play, pause, toggle, stop, seek, or run an action. The hub cards and this button are written that way.
any DOM event name; run arguments must be compile-time values; the action starts with eventTarget, eventKey and its arguments — nothing from the surrounding block
on key binds keyboard shortcuts — Escape takes you to the hub, space pauses, r replays, in every chapter.
a KeyboardController; unknown names are errors; input fields are ignored
Under both forms sits a controller: lasting behaviour attached to a selected element. This is what on click desugars to — one of nine.
DOMEventListener · Keyboard · Label · Lottie · MutationObserver · Navigation · Progressbar · Routing · Subtitles
locales make text translatable: a LabelController renders a key in the active language. This label — and the hub title — are real ones: click nl-NL and it switches.
completion and did-you-mean on the key; Chapter 07 has the editor
Your own JavaScript reaches in too: a host operation is called like a built-in. This clock was stamped by host.js just now.
bundled by --bundle, dev, smoke and the preview (trusted workspaces)
Eventbus, on event, interactions, controllers, locales, host code — the hub, its title and every click you made were built from these. Hub.

The other half of Eligian is the editor. Install the extension and every .eligian file gets highlighting, checking, completion, hover, a preview — all of which wrote this tour. What follows is a mock-up with the real texts.
one extension: highlighting, diagnostics, completion, hovers, preview, Timeline view, Locale Editor
Syntax errors speak plainly, and every semantic rule — imports, names, arguments, events, timelines — lands in Problems while you type.
one line per syntax error: a keyword used as a name is explained, expected tokens read as words
Every class and selector is checked against your CSS and your layout — even when it travels through an action parameter. Typo one: a squiggle, a suggestion, a one-click fix.
CSS ∪ layout for selectors; CSS only for class names · eligian.validation.selectorNotInLayout
The dataflow check knows what each block carries. A missing selected element gets a fix: Insert selectElement, or Add target.
an action's hover lists what it needs from the caller
Type and the editor knows what fits: operations, your actions, controllers, CSS classes and ids, DOM events, keys, timeline names, label keys, even whole event skeletons.
the list depends on the place: a call, a navigate target, a key, a controller name
Inside a call the signature follows your cursor; resolved times and parameter names sit in the code as inlay hints.
settings: eligian.inlayHints.*
Hover anything: an operation's docs from Eligius, your action's JSDoc, the CSS rule behind a class. Type /** above an action and the template writes itself.
call: the JSDoc · definition: what call sites are checked for · timeline: its header
F12 jumps from navigate to the timeline, from a selector to the CSS rule or the layout element. Shift+F12 finds references across .eligian, CSS and HTML; F2 renames a timeline everywhere.
eligian.codeLens.cssReferences · Find Eligian References in CSS and HTML files
The Outline lists timelines with their lifecycle blocks and events at their resolved times — Ctrl+Shift+O jumps to any beat.
also the breadcrumbs and Go to Symbol

Snippets scaffold an action, a timeline, a chapter. Format Document tidies whitespace only. And every start and end block is labelled in the margin; a range rewrites itself as start for duration in one click.
the same rules as eligian fmt

Ctrl+K V opens the preview: the real engine in a webview, recompiled on every save and keeping its place; CSS, layout, locale and host-module edits reload live. Scrub, pick a timeline or a language, or start from a line.
eligian.preview.highlightActiveEvents · eligian.codeLens.preview

An engine error during preview becomes a diagnostic on the operation that failed, with Go to Source; a compile error shows in the preview, with Retry Compilation. And Eligius' own lint runs 200 ms after you stop typing.
source 'eligius-runtime' / 'Eligius lint'; setting eligian.validation.eligiusLint

The Eligian panel draws each timeline as a Gantt chart: a bar per event at its resolved time, the preview's playhead moving through. Click a bar to jump to its source; double-click to preview from there.
bars named by their labels; stagger rows by their item
Edit translations in the Locale Editor — Ctrl+Click the locales path, or Open With. New Presentation writes a starter project; Compile Current File writes the JSON beside your file.
label quick fixes: Create labels file · Create label entry 'hub.title' · Use '<key>'
Ten settings tune it: lint, selector checks, playhead highlights, CodeLenses, inlay hints. Concise, checked, live — that's Eligian in the editor. Hub.
Settings › Extensions › Eligian
The compiler is also a command: eligian on npm, Node 22.12 or later. Install it, or run it once with npx.
two bins: eligian and eligian-cli · -V / --version · -h / --help · help [command]
eligian init writes a starter that already checks clean: blank, chapters, video or library, with layout, styles, locales, a package.json and a README.
-t / --template · --title (default: from the directory name) · --force overwrites
eligian file.eligian compiles to Eligius JSON next to the file. Dash o picks the output, dash for stdout; --check only validates; --minify, --no-optimize, -q and -v adjust the rest.
-o - writes the JSON to stdout · eligian file is short for eligian compile file
--bundle writes a standalone presentation: index.html, bundle.js, your assets, small images inlined, only the Eligius pieces you use. --force overwrites, --sourcemap and --inline-threshold tune it.
next to the input as tour.bundle/, or -o a directory · --inline-threshold in bytes (51200 by default)

--eligian-map also writes the map from every compiled action and operation back to its source line — the same map the preview and smoke build in memory to point at the failing operation, written to a file for your own tools.
compiled actions and operations → .eligian source locations
eligian check reports every error and warning of many files — globs, directories, exclusions — and fails on warnings when you tell it to.
patterns: files, directories, globs, !excludes; node_modules skipped

Four output formats: pretty, json, sarif for code scanning, github for pull-request annotations. Eligius' own configuration lint runs too unless --no-lint; --selector-not-in-layout adds the layout check.
sarif 2.1.0 · github workflow commands
eligian smoke plays every timeline headlessly on the real engine: enter, every start and end, leave — and reports what fails at its source line. --strict also flags selectors that match nothing.
--strict: selectElement selectors that match no element · --format pretty, github or json
eligian dev serves the bundle and rebuilds on every change: a CSS edit swaps styles in place, anything else reloads and resumes at the same position. Build errors show as an overlay.
only files under the entry's directory are watched · a taken --port moves to the next free one
eligian fmt checks formatting — whitespace only, the editor's Format Document rules — and --write applies it. CI runs it on every example.
--format text or github · a file with syntax errors is left alone (exit 2)

Exit codes you can script on: 0 clean, 1 findings or a failed compile, 2 usage errors of check, smoke, fmt, dev and init, 3 I/O. The repo's CI checks, plays and format-checks every example this way. Hub.
commander's own usage errors (a missing argument, an unknown option) exit 1
